assertion_results.text: Tasks target both 'trustify-backend' and 'trustify-ui' repositories with at least one task per repo
assertion_results.evidence: Tasks 1, 2, 7 target trustify-backend. Tasks 3, 4, 5, 6 target trustify-ui. Both repositories have multiple tasks.

assertion_results.text: Backend tasks have lower task numbers than the frontend tasks that depend on them
assertion_results.evidence: Backend tasks are Task 1 and Task 2. Frontend Task 3 depends on Task 2 (backend), Task 4 depends on Task 3, Task 5 depends on Task 4, Task 6 depends on Tasks 4 and 5. All backend tasks (1, 2) have lower numbers than the frontend tasks (3, 4, 5, 6) that transitively depend on them. Task 7 is documentation and depends on all prior tasks.

assertion_results.text: UI-facing frontend tasks (pages, components) reference Figma design context mentioning specific PatternFly components and visual specifications — API-layer frontend tasks (API types, client functions, hooks) are exempt from this requirement
assertion_results.evidence: Task 3 (API types, client function, hook) is exempt as an API-layer task. Task 4 (comparison page) has extensive Figma design references including PatternFly Select, ExpandableSection, Badge, Table, EmptyState, Dropdown, Skeleton with visual specs (colors, column definitions, layout, empty state design). assertion_results.text: Every generated task description contains a Target Branch section — either all set to 'main' (direct-to-main workflow) or bookend tasks set to 'main' with intermediate tasks set to the feature issue ID (feature-branch workflow)
assertion_results.evidence: All 7 tasks have '## Target Branch\nmain'. The impact-map.md confirms 'Selected mode: direct-to-main' with rationale 'All tasks target branch main with sequential dependencies ensuring correct merge order.' This is a consistent direct-to-main workflow.

assertion_results.text: For each task created, a description digest is produced — evidenced by a separate digest file (e.g., task-N-digest.md), a digest entry in the impact map, or a '[sdlc-workflow] Description digest: sha256-md:<64-char-hex>' marker in any output file. The digest must contain a format-tagged SHA-256 hash — exactly 64 lowercase hex characters prefixed by 'sha256-md:' or 'sha256-adf:'
assertion_results.evidence: All 7 digest files (task-1-digest.md through task-7-digest.md) exist but contain placeholder text: '[sdlc-workflow] Description digest: sha256-md:<computed-after-jira-creation>'. The value '<computed-after-jira-creation>' is not a valid 64-character lowercase hex SHA-256 hash. The assertion requires 'exactly 64 lowercase hex characters prefixed by sha256-md: or sha256-adf:' and the placeholder does not satisfy this.

Task 4: 'Applies: task creates src/pages/SbomComparePage/SbomComparePage.tsx matching the convention's .tsx page file scope.' Task 5: 'Applies: task modifies src/pages/SbomListPage/SbomListPage.tsx matching the convention's .tsx component file scope.' Task 6: 'Applies: task creates src/pages/SbomComparePage/SbomComparePage.test.tsx matching the convention's .tsx test file scope.' No inapplicable conventions are listed with 'Not applicable' annotations anywhere.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a priority set (not 'Undefined'), the plan documents that the Feature's priority is inherited by created tasks — evidenced by priority field values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When the Feature's priority is 'Undefined', the plan documents that priority inheritance is skipped (not propagated as null or 'Undefined')
assertion_results.evidence: Impact-map.md Task Creation section: '"priority": {"name": "Critical"}' and 'priority: inherited from Feature TC-9003 (Critical). Not "Undefined", so it is propagated.' Summary-comment.md: 'Priority: Critical (propagated from Feature TC-9003 to all Epics and Tasks)'. The Feature priority is Critical (not Undefined) and the plan documents propagation.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a non-empty fixVersions array and the fixVersion scope config (from ### Jira Field Defaults in CLAUDE.md) is 'task' or 'both' (or absent, defaulting to 'both'), the plan documents that fixVersions are inherited by created tasks — evidenced by fixVersion values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When fixVersion scope is 'feature' or the Feature has no fixVersions, the plan documents that fixVersion inheritance is skipped
assertion_results.evidence: Impact-map.md: '"fixVersions": [{"name": "RHTPA 1.5.0"}]' and 'fixVersions: inherited from Feature TC-9003 (RHTPA 1.5.0). The fixVersion scope setting is absent from Jira Field Defaults (no ### Jira Field Defaults section in CLAUDE.md), so the default "both" applies — fixVersions are propagated to tasks.' Summary-comment.md: 'fixVersions: RHTPA 1.5.0 (propagated from Feature TC-9003 to all Epics and Tasks; fixVersion scope defaults to "both" since no Jira Field Defaults section exists)'. The fixVersion scope is absent (defaults to 'both') and fixVersions are non-empty, so inheritance is correctly documented.

assertion_results.text: A summary of inherited field propagation is produced — evidenced by a summary-comment.md file in the outputs directory, or a summary section in the impact map that includes the inherited priority and fixVersion values propagated to tasks, or states they were omitted and why
